newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU-U.S. Blair House deal under attack in Germany.
newsitem.headline: EU-U.S. Blair House deal under attack in Germany.

text.p: The leader of Germany's farm union and a prominent oilseeds processor criticised the limits imposed on European Union production by the Blair House accord between the U.S. and the EU.
The agreement, which dates back to 1992, helped finalise the GATT world trade round by imposing limits on EU oilseeds production.

Arnd von Wissel, chairman of Oelmuehle Hamburg (Oelag), told a shareholders meeting on Friday, "We criticise the rigid volume restrictions of the agreement because they mean the EU has no chance of participating in the expansion of international oilseeds demand."
Margins at Oelag in 1996 suffered because of the high cost of domestic rapeseed, he said.
This was caused by the EU volume restrictions and supply shortfalls resulting from severe winter damage. Oil and meal earnings by the mills were unsatisfactory, he said.
Oelag overcame the problems by switching its facilities to soybeans, helped by modern plant equipment and its location on the river Elbe, which allowed imports via the North Sea.

But this was not an option for land-locked plants specialising in soft seeds. Oelag also opposed Blair House because it limited the amount of industrial oilseeds crops grown on set-aside land, where Oelag has an interest in rapeseed supply to feed its biofuel facilities.
Gerd Sonnleitner, the president of German farm union DBV, in a separate statement issued during DBV's annual general meeting said the Blair House deal needed to be reviewed.

"It can't be right for the U.S. to increase their oilseeds production by an amount equalling total EU output while we can't even keep up the production and marketing of renewable crops because of the Blair House limit," Sonnleitner said.
